choices: Port source1 complete USB19000/HDD19001 switches: sixteen one-item stick slots or one sixteen-file drive, selected mode, tier-gated read/write/clear, held-stick copy, loaded adjacent cable reads with optional gt.usb.dir, six selector covers/control, ordinary menus, complete data tooltips and inventory persistence. Reuse twelve existing technological media IDs, without duplicating item/material registries. Native CUSTOM_DATA writes explicitly commit detached tags and preserve unrelated fields; stack/provider block persistence uses native APIs.

Install all three full dynamic material-data providers in native recipe loading: molecular scanner exact-medium replacement; printer material-dictionary output, paper/dye counts and retained medium; replicator nucleon fluids/energy, original form preference/counts, fluid fallback and retained stick/cable. Native MachineContextRecipes now performs actual adjacent USB lookup rather than an unbound boundary. Both platforms consume shared keys/tier/slot/mode, work coefficients and form/count catalog. Previous dictionaries, fluids, materials and full recipe map contract are reused.

brokestar uses the same opaque file keys/components but distinct gt6 item identities and exact T3 scanner membership. Its scanner duration/power distribution, SCANNABLE and UUM flags, priority prefix and room-temperature replication differ from source1. Preserve current full baseline behavior; those domain differences are explicit later decisions, not silently copied across different unit/flag systems. masson PrinterPrepSpec explicitly says unregistered prep-only, so it cannot replace a working runtime provider.

Port source1 twelve extender identities: four legacy opposite-face inventory/fluid relays and eight actual double-facing/straight-across inventory/tank/combined/universal variants. Full live sided capabilities, loaded-only target resolution and cycle guards forward into current neighboring handlers. Universal variants also forward GT signed packets, external FE, machine modes/state/progress and redstone/comparator signals. All local covers persist/drop/render; item/fluid shutter checks are retained. Shared routing and per-operation visit-set lifecycle are consumed on both platforms. masson live fluid extender matches opposing target but also actively pumps fluid each tick; retain non-buffered baseline relay semantics while that distinct pumping policy stays pending. No filename or search-match for independent brokestar extender/filter classes was found; this is not proof of absence across every generalized class.

Port four full filters (items/fluids/combined/prefix), fifty-four ghost templates or one selected-prefix template, blacklist/whitelist, screwdriver/soft-hammer/wrench controls, dual facing and packed filter state. Native ghost menu carries prefix mode and cannot extract templates. Existing Native FilterRules supports canonical forms/portable cells/pipe sizes and forge/c tags. Full native fluid-display binding resolves original metadata items and lossless external-fluid/components payload, using explicit registry providers. Both platforms now consume shared ghost count and matching/blacklist policies.

Port six EU automatic igniters and four signed-KU automatic hammers with complete source1 input/quality/hardness identities, facing/wrench/stop controls, work/cooldown NBT and ordinary ticks. Native burning-box entities now implement the actual powered-target interface over their existing ignition methods. Shared profiles/work cap/budgets and timing are consumed by both platforms. masson automatic hammer has more faithful bronze/steel/tungstensteel naming, pending tick explosion scaling, anvil-context/harvest/drop-conversion behavior. Preserve current baseline IDs rather than silently remap materials; these additional behaviors remain pending. Shared magnitude comparison also avoids Math.abs(Long.MIN_VALUE) overflow, while packet guards still reject invalid input.
knownGaps: Grouped dual compilation covers all28 block variants and dynamic recipe APIs. No new fixture added. One grouped ordinary native dedicated startup is pending and will cover previous202 storage/chest/garbage variants too; it does not prove placed interaction or recipe execution.

Baseline molecular scanner accepts every registered primary material, not original per-prefix SCANNABLE, and tier3/4 sticks. Replicator lacks original UUM gate/priority prefix/room-temperature-fluid preference; printer outputs a bound dictionary instead of printed pages. Those source differences remain explicit. Other USB data types and wider scanner/map/blueprint printer behavior still need integration.

Original direct material-data convenience readers and generic tier-gated port reads have different file-tier checks; signed legacy tier bytes and material short IDs are preserved at their original boundaries. Component data/save migration and actual cable/cover selection after restart are unverified.

Four legacy extenders expose identical basic opposing relay behavior despite names including wireless; they are not claimed to implement wireless range. Full source extender/bridge redstone and FE reentrancy, unloaded targets and filter packed state are unverified. Universal cover shutter applies to item/fluid forwarding as in baseline; broader energy gating remains pending.
Native FluidDisplayBinding is a real filter resolver/payload API; actual external fluid display creation/render/subtype and JEI consumption remain unverified.

Automatic hammer native anvil/manual processing utility block targets remain unported. Fallback hammer harvest retains baseline no-block-entity/pickaxe gate and vanilla drops, not masson broader crush conversions. Source1 instant fixed-strength overvoltage differs from masson queued tier-strength explosions. No auto-tool gameplay or energy chain has been exercised.
Client/rendering, Forge runtime, complete survival chain, independent saved-world restart/old saves and production jars remain pending. Publication authorization is unchanged; full goal stays active.
